organizations.What they build: Alphabet's AI lab (HQ London). Builds the Gemini Robotics family: a vision-language-action model (VLA = a model that turns camera images + a text instruction into motor commands), an embodied-reasoning model for multi-step planning, and an on-device VLA. Gemini Robotics 2.5 (Nov 2026) reports 30-100% higher success than the previous version, tested on Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid and in a Mercedes-Benz factory pilot.

End-to-end 'embodied AI' for driving: one learned model drives the car from camera input instead of hand-written rules. Partnering with Uber for a London robotaxi service (initially with safety drivers) and with Mercedes-Benz and Nissan on driver assistance. Offices in UK, US, Canada, Germany; reports $2.8B total funding in 4 rounds on its site, plus a $1.2B+ raise in Feb 2026 per press.

Open-source AI hub. Its LeRobot library (launched May 2024, co-founded by Rémi Cadène; now led by Steven Palma) covers the whole robot-learning loop: teleoperate a robot, record datasets, train imitation/RL policies (e.g. SmolVLA, ACT), deploy. Ships low-cost open hardware: SO-101 arm and Reachy Mini (~$299 kit, from its Pollen Robotics acquisition). Nvidia agreed in Sept 2026 to buy Hugging Face for ~$12.9B; the US DOJ is reviewing, close expected H1 2027.
organizations.Warm contact path: Paris office; LeRobot Discord and GitHub community; LeRobot hackathon organizers

organizations.What they build: Frontier AI lab founded by Yann LeCun (ex-Meta FAIR, Turing Award). Builds 'world models' (JEPA-style: predict the future in an abstract representation space rather than pixel by pixel) so agents can plan actions; targets industrial control, automation, wearables and robotics. Raised a ~$1.03B seed in March 2026 (investors incl. Cathay Innovation, Greycroft, Hiro, NVIDIA, SBVA, Bezos, Schmidt).

Founded early 2025; raised a $105M seed (Eclipse, Khosla, Eric Schmidt) to build robot foundation models trained largely in simulation (it originated the open-source Genesis physics simulator). In June 2026 it unveiled Eno, a non-humanoid general-purpose robot (wheeled base, foldable tower, human-like hands) running its own model (GENE-26.5 announced May 2026). Customer deployments targeted end of 2026.

Founded 2021 by Univ. of Stuttgart AI researchers. Hardware-agnostic 'robot brain' software: the Cortex foundation model takes natural-language instructions and outputs actions for arms, mobile manipulators and humanoids. Cortex 2.0 adds a world model that simulates candidate motions and scores them before acting. Raised $110M Series B (Apr 2026); customers include BMW, Zalando, CEVA.

Polish 'physical AI' for warehouse picking: its AI brain plus vision lets robot arms pick millions of different items. Zalando is rolling out up to 50 Nomagic robots across European fulfilment centres (Mar 2026), including a shoebox picker. Expanding in the US.

UK humanoid company building wheel-based industrial humanoids and the KinetIQ AI framework for fleet-level control and RL-based skill learning. Raised $152M Series A at $1.35B valuation (Jul 2026, led by Prime Movers Lab; Schaeffler, Bosch participate); total funding $270M; customer beta rollouts from Q4 2026.

Founded by former Nvidia researchers; builds a 'brain' for humanoids: low-level skills (walking, stairs, opening doors, carrying) trained in simulation with reinforcement learning, plus a higher-level model trained on human videos that picks which skill to run. Aims for one model deployable on any robot body. Raised a ~$50M Series A (Nov 2025, per press).

ETH Zurich spin-off doing end-to-end learning for dexterous manipulation (human-like robotic hands) in factories: assembly, kitting, cables, soft objects. In July 2026 introduced FLUX-mimic, a video-action model built with Black Forest Labs that learns tasks from video with far less demonstration data, deployed at Audi.

Robot-data startup founded by ex-Red Bull and Mercedes F1 engineers. Its Atlas platform records how humans and robots do real factory tasks (dedicated recording hardware + secure data platform) to train and deploy robots in production. Raised a $55M (≈€48M) seed in July 2026, described as Germany's largest; partners with Google Cloud.

Cloud platform for robot learning: collect teleoperation demonstrations, version datasets, train imitation/RL policies, deploy and monitor on real robots. Free for academic users (sign-up with academic email); open-source client tools. $3M pre-seed led by Earlybird (Nov 2025).

Open-source (MIT) data layer for physical AI: an SDK to log, store, query, visualize and stream multimodal robot data (cameras, point clouds, joint states) for debugging and training. Rerun Hub is the commercial catalog. Remote-first Swedish company; raised a $17M seed (Mar 2025, per press).

Robot programming software: NOVA, a robot-agnostic 'operating system' that connects digital twins/simulation (e.g. NVIDIA Isaac Sim) to real industrial robots so tasks can be designed in simulation and deployed the same day. Customers/partners reported include Volkswagen Sachsen and Schaeffler.

AI vision-and-control software MIRAI that lets industrial robots handle variation (position, shape, light, reflective/transparent objects) by learning from human demonstrations. Founded in Berlin by Ronnie Vuine; reorganized as a US-based company in 2024 (per press headline).

3D vision + hardware-agnostic AI software that lets existing industrial robots (FANUC, ABB, KUKA, Yaskawa, Comau, Universal Robots) see part positions and correct their motions in real time. Deployed on 200+ robots in 100+ factories (Stellantis, Toyota, Ford, Bosch). Raised $12.5M in Sept 2026 (total $34M).

Lausanne startup (launched Sept 2026, round led by Faber VC, amount undisclosed) building an 'Embodied AI flywheel': task-specific AI models + teleoperation data collection + its own robots for electronics, kitting, cable handling and automotive assembly. Unveiled AIR, a wheeled humanoid that learns on the job (Nov 2026, per press headlines).

Paris startup building AI models/software to deploy industrial humanoid robots, aiming to cut the full deployment process to one hour or less (reports teaching a new gesture with ~10 demonstrations). €5M pre-seed (Oct 2026, Contrarian Ventures and OVNI Capital).

Prof. Marco Hutter's lab: legged robots (origin of ANYmal / ANYbotics) and robot learning, notably RL for locomotion and manipulation; publishes open-source code such as the RSL-RL library and world-model methods for humanoid locomotion.
European branch (led by Fraunhofer IPA) of the ROS-Industrial consortium, which extends ROS/ROS 2 open-source software to industrial robots; runs trainings and conferences for members.

summary: Leaders: Google DeepMind (Gemini Robotics 2.5 VLA) and Hugging Face (LeRobot, open source) set the agenda; Wayve leads embodied AI for driving.
Money: 2026 mega-rounds went to world models and robot brains - AMI ~$1.03B seed (Paris), Wayve $1.2B+, Humanoid $152M, Sereact $110M, Genesis AI $105M seed, microagi $55M seed.
Demand: factories and warehouses (BMW, Zalando, Audi, Stellantis, Mercedes) are paying for hardware-agnostic AI layers on existing robots, not new hardware.
Hypothesis check: the slice supports our wedge - imitation learning, VLAs, sim-to-real and robot-data tooling are exactly where European money and talent are going.
Best entry point: Hugging Face LeRobot in Paris (hackathons, hardware, Hub visibility), then free tools from Neuracore/Rerun and Paris startups Bleu Robotics, Genesis AI and Inbolt for talks.
